row.locator:
| 12 | **TILE** — `dstW = floor(slack/numStretch / srcW) * srcW` (whole tiles) | `0x5266`-`0x5292` |
| 8, 11, 18 | **STRETCH (grow)** — `share = sVar5/sVar6 + slack/numStretch` | `0x529e`-`0x52d6` |
| 13, 14 | **STRETCH** smaller share (`sVar5/sVar6`, no slack term) | `0x52da`-`0x52f8` |
| else | call `0x49d6(pc,flag)`: nonzero → leave width 0 (budget participant); else FIXED `dstW=srcW`; **except** pc∈{5,6} AND flag==0 → width 0 (collapse) | `0x52fc`-`0x532a` |

So **codes 5/6** (title bezel) are FIXED when the title fits (`flag`=`fp@(-290)`
title-fits, pushed at `0x5100`/`0x5120`) and **collapse to 0** when it doesn't —
they never grow. Budget = `slack = (srcBorder[end]−srcBorder[start-1]) − reqWidth`
(`0x518a`); the primary divisor counts only 8/11/12/18 (`0x4b3e`), while 8/11/13/14/18
share the division and whole-tile remainder. Each remainder share is truncated
against the number of recipients still to visit, so extra pixels accumulate at
the END of the walk (3/3/4 for a budget of 10 and three ordinary growers)
row.claim: Two-pass per-half allocation: primary 8/11/12/18, whole-tile truncation, remainder to 8/11/13/14/18 toward the end; 0x49d6 stretch verdicts leave width 0.
row.limits: Within one half of a given extent with a nonnegative budget. Title-anchor half extents, codes 5/6 (title-fits flag, 0x5312), widget flag values and below-minimum behaviour are not established.

row.claim: Every sliced window type, both states, 15 sampled content sizes: END-based cells, 1:1 leading corner, flag-independent part-code widths, per-half 0x5178 allocation (nonnegative budgets; observed titled-half extent) and opaque pixels of 1px-run non-18 cells (direction-independent; runtime cross-axis placement); zero failures, nonvacuous counts.

transitions.summary: PR #412 (merged as 9eeab416) ledger transition, per the Tier-2 review's ledgerProposal. The five <slug>.window.corner-sprite cases are narrowed to the procedural-frame document family (options.windowTypes; substitution restated as declared slug → variation policy, §10.3). New assertion window.procedural-frame (tests/rendering-options/procedural-frame.spec.mjs, source and built) binds DRIVER_ROWS D4/D6 to public renderWindow. window.wnd-ladder (5) and window.corner-sprite-frame (5) unknown -> verified at engine level under the declared environment; window.state-frame unknown -> verified for black-platinum, platinum-8, slimes and system7-nostalgia-silver (4) and kept unknown for apple-platinum-2, whose -14332 and -14336 are pixel-identical (selection-non-discriminating). fill.remaining and window.masked-composition stay unknown with updated rationales; the 25 window.procedural-* rows keep their status with the stale 'no driver yet' sentence replaced. Evidence kdef.procedural-frame-gate gains window.wnd-ladder; -geometry and -frame-lines gain window.corner-sprite-frame. Five new cases <slug>.window.procedural-frame-utility (25 assessments, all unknown, issue #414; spec rev 3 in PR #415 decodes the utility frame). Every case closure stays OPEN.
transitions.review: Independent automated Tier-2 review (campaign-20261021 v2-lanes/family2/IMPL-REVIEW.json, reviewed head ce3c428c): procedural-frame document family re-traced and verified at engine level under declared environment; utility frame undecoded (Q1), stays unknown. The window.procedural-frame browser assertion is new in this transition and binds the reviewed D4/D6 rule rows to public renderWindow; apple-platinum-2 state-frame departs from the proposal (non-discriminating). Revised after REVIEW-418 (campaign-20261021 v2-lanes/family2/REVIEW-418.json, reviewed head c2fc8028, CHANGES-REQUIRED, no status change): B1 the §1.1 gate now reads the raw fork in the page; B2 inactive widget absence is checked in all three slots; B3 the masked-composition rationale no longer claims the mask is tested.

transitions.priorScope: Ledger rows owned by the window family (case families: window-chrome): the single-file ledger 1.22.0 rows, with at 1.1.0 (main 1.24.0, #377) the code-10 corrections, at 1.2.0 the five corner-sprite cases extended with five procedural-frame requirements, and at 1.3.0 (#412) those five cases narrowed to the procedural-frame document family with wnd-ladder, corner-sprite-frame and (four archives) state-frame verified at engine level, plus five unknown procedural-frame utility cases (#414). Every case closure remains OPEN.

row.claim: For each of the five archives whose raw resource fork (sit-wasm + parseResourceFork, read in the page) ships no wnd# and no WDEF -14330, with the 1138 fork as the wnd# negative control, public renderWindow draws an active and an inactive 200 × 140 document window whose structure is 213 × 169, whose DRIVER_ROWS D4 port probes equal the -14332 (active) / -14336 (inactive) frame cicn sample points or stay untouched, and whose D6 widget slots carry the close -14336, zoom -14334 and collapse -14335 ics8 pixels wherever the ics# mask is set. When inactive, none of the three slots shows any glyph pixel that differs from the -14336 title fill P(6, 3) (each slot has such pixels). Only mask-set pixels are compared; mask-clear pixels are not checked. The frame-state probes discriminate on every archive except apple-platinum-2, whose two frame cicns are pixel-identical.

transitions.summary: Records the #421 utility-frame ledger change proposed by its Tier-2 review (IMPL-REVIEW-421.json round-2 ledgerProposal, head 9a28dd48; #421 merged into v2 as 296f7284). New browser assertion window.procedural-frame-utility (source and built) and four utility evidence rows (kdef.procedural-frame-utility-gate, -art, -geometry, -frame-lines). The five <slug>.window.procedural-frame-utility cases list the five reachable utility types by canonical slug and exclude collapsed-no-title-utility-window (#423). Promoted unknown -> verified (engine level, declared environment): window.wnd-ladder and window.corner-sprite-frame for all five archives, window.state-frame for black-platinum, platinum-8, slimes and system7-nostalgia-silver (14 rows). apple-platinum-2 state-frame stays unknown (pixel-identical frames); fill.remaining and window.masked-composition stay unknown. All 25 rows now cite #423 instead of the closed #414. Reviewed by REVIEW-424.json (Tier 2, head 33bd612a); its non-blocking N4 adds window.procedural-frame (raw-fork wnd# gate) to the five utility wnd-ladder rows and that assertion's caseIds, N3 adds the inactive no-title interior check to window.procedural-frame-utility, and N6 rewords the title substitution as runtime policy.
transitions.review: Independent automated Tier-2 review (campaign-20261021 v2-lanes/family2/REVIEW-424.json, reviewed head 33bd612a): window.procedural-frame-utility (source and built) fails under 13 of 17 reviewer runtime mutations, every promoted geometry, routing and state claim among them; grow box, widget box position and no-title title absence are covered only at engine level or not at all and are not claimed; wnd-ladder and corner-sprite-frame verified for five archives and state-frame for four at engine level under declared environment; apple-platinum-2 state, fill and masked composition stay unknown; 257/33/1542 of 1832.

transitions.priorScope: Ledger rows owned by the window family (case families: window-chrome): the single-file ledger 1.22.0 rows, with at 1.1.0 (main 1.24.0, #377) the code-10 corrections, at 1.2.0 the five corner-sprite cases extended with five procedural-frame requirements, at 1.3.0 (#412) those five cases narrowed to the procedural-frame document family with wnd-ladder, corner-sprite-frame and (four archives) state-frame verified at engine level, plus five unknown procedural-frame utility cases (#414), and at 1.4.0 (#421) the utility cases' wnd-ladder, corner-sprite-frame and (four archives) state-frame verified at engine level through window.procedural-frame-utility, collapsed-no-title excluded (#423). Every case closure remains OPEN.

row.claim: Walk each side-list END-based (0x5356) with [0,border[0]) as a 1:1 corner, and size flag-independent part codes 0/1/7/8/9/11/12/13/14/18 within each half by the two-pass 0x5178 allocation, for nonnegative budgets; titled-half allocation is checked given the observed half extent, and halves are split at the runtime 5/6 run rather than the decode code-5 anchor.
Place the title anchor and both half extents (0x4a64, 0x4fa8..0x50fa), including windows below the fixed-art minimum, as the original engine does.

Every sliced window type, both states, 24 sampled content sizes (template + {-12,0,1,2,7,97} x {-12,0,1,33}, clamped at 0): END-based cells, 1:1 leading corner, flag-independent part-code widths, code 10 fixed unless the 0x4e0e too-short verdict holds (then 0; unknown when widget-gated codes straddle it), per-half 0x5178 allocation (nonnegative budgets; observed titled-half extent) and opaque pixels of 1px-run non-18 cells (direction-independent; runtime cross-axis placement); zero failures, nonvacuous counts.

transitions.summary: Window-recipe migration (#432, window-widgets.md merged in #420, answers in #437, wording #445): window.recipe-cells and window.half-extent re-worded to the decoded rows at the declared defaults and verified for the 13 wnd# cases; flag-gated-parts, masked-composition and fill.remaining re-judged and kept unknown (F7 widget flags; code-18 scale mapping, Q3). Nine window-widgets evidence rows added; window.recipe-rules now replays the full layout (including the TT2a default), WD4 and WD6 pixels and HT hits with in-page mutation bites.
transitions.review: Reviewed 2026-10-23 by the independent automated Tier-2 verifier (Claude), REVIEW-432-444 round 2 (PRs #432 28b9295f, #444 aa0ba8f6): rule model re-derived from window-widgets.md and re-traced against the 2.3.1 kDEF listing (24 rows); 15 of 17 valid runtime mutations caught by the rule specs in source and built mode, the TT2a default included (the other 2, title-text placement, are outside these requirements and caught only by the goldens); promotion of window.recipe-cells and window.half-extent for the 13 wnd# cases accepted.

transitions.priorScope: Ledger rows owned by the window family (case families: window-chrome): the single-file ledger 1.22.0 rows, with at 1.1.0 (main 1.24.0, #377) the code-10 corrections, at 1.2.0 the five corner-sprite cases extended with five procedural-frame requirements, at 1.3.0 (#412) those five cases narrowed to the procedural-frame document family, at 1.4.0 (#424) the utility frame bound to rule rows, and at 1.5.0 (#432) the 13 wnd# cases re-judged against docs/spec/engine/window-widgets.md: recipe-cells and half-extent verified at the §2.3 declared defaults. Every case closure remains OPEN.

row.locator:
| TT1 | always | `Fb` (`Fa`) = Σ `w(i)` over segments *i* < `anchor` (> `anchor`) with `V(code, drop)` = keep and code ∉ {8, 11, 12, 13, 14, 18}. Codes 5/6 count here; code 10 does not once `drop = 1` | `0x4e54..0x4eec` |
| TT2 | `R = E − Fb − Fa < W` | `W −= SW − SWc`, where `SWc` is StringWidth(title) measured with `$A888` TextFace condense (32), or bold + condense (33) under `altWidgets`; the face is then set back to plain (0), or bold (1) under `altWidgets` | `0x4eee..0x4f42` |
| TT2a | (runtime value of `SWc`) | **declared default** (modern policy, not decoded: the width comes from the Font Manager, not the kDEF): `SWc = SW − titleLen`, Apple's synthetic condense of one pixel less per character (Inside Macintosh: Text, Font Manager style extra). Not observed for Charcoal or Virtue; a measured condensed width replaces it. `SWc = SW` makes TT2 inert and is a divergence, not this default | Inside Macintosh: Text |
| TT3 | `R ≤ 2` | `titleLen = 0`, `W = 0` | `0x4f46..0x4f62` |
| TT4 | `titleLen = 0` (by TS1, TT3 or an untitled window, TT10) | if segment `anchor+1` is code 6, `Fa −=` its width; if segment `anchor−1` is code 6, `Fb −=` its width | `0x4f66..0x4fa4` |
| TT4a | `anchor = 1` or `anchor = N` | the code TT4 reads for "segment `anchor−1`" is entry 0's code in the placed list, and for "segment `anchor+1`" the slot after entry `N`. The layout writes neither slot, so what they hold is **not decoded**. Declared default: no subtraction. No corpus side has its anchor at 1 or `N` (§6.2) | `0x4f6c..0x4f96` |
| TT5 | always | `P[anchor−1] = P[0] + Fb`; `P[anchor] = P[N] − Fa` | `0x4fa8..0x4fcc` |
| TT6 | `growersBefore > 0`, `growersAfter > 0` and `Fb > Fa` | `L = mid − (W + (T4.left − S[anchor−1]) + (T4.right − S[anchor])) / 2`; if `L > P[anchor−1]`, `P[anchor−1] = L`. Then if `P[anchor−1] + W < P[anchor]`, `P[anchor] = P[anchor−1] + W` | `0x4fd0..0x5046` |
| TT7 | otherwise | if `growersAfter > 0`: `R' = mid + (W + (S[anchor] − T4.right) + (S[anchor−1] − T4.left)) / 2` when `growersBefore > 0`, else `R' = P[anchor−1] + W`; if `R' < P[anchor]`, `P[anchor] = R'`. Then, if `growersBefore > 0`: if `P[anchor] − W > P[anchor−1]`, `P[anchor−1] = P[anchor] − W` | `0x5048..0x50ba` |
| TT8 | `W < 0` | `P[anchor−1] −= S[anchor−1] − T4.left`, `Fb −=` the same; `P[anchor] −= S[anchor] − T4.right`, `Fa +=` the same; then the working template borders `S[anchor−1]`, `S[anchor]` become `T4.left`, `T4.right` for the rest of this message | `0x50be..0x50fa` |
| TT9 | always | two allocations: segments `1..anchor−1` (required `Fb`, primary count `growersBefore`) and `anchor+1..N` (required `Fa`, `growersAfter`), both with the side's `drop` and the title gate `titleLen` | `0x5100..0x513c` |
| TT10 | untitled window (`titleLen = 0`, `SW = 0`, no drop) | the same rows as after a drop, except `W`: TT4 removes the code-6 neighbours from `Fb`/`Fa`, and TT9's gate 0 gives every 5/6 segment inside the two allocations width 0 (AW5), so the **bezels are not drawn**. The anchor (plate) cell is **not** forced to 0: `W = (T4.left − S[anchor−1]) + (S[anchor] − T4.right)` (LS6 with `SW = 0`), and TT6/TT7 cap the cell at that width when either half has a primary grower. It is 0 where the two margins sum to 0 (`T4` fills the cell, or is shifted inside it as on monkey-paradise movable-modal), positive where `T4` is narrower, and negative where `T4` overhangs it, which runs TT8 | `0x4a94..0x4aa6`, `0x4b20..0x4b3a`, `0x4f66`, `0x530c` |
row.claim: The titled side: Fb/Fa, condense (TT2), title drop at ≤ 2 px (TT3), bezel removal for an untitled or dropped title (TT4, TT10), anchor placement on the content-rect centre (TT5–TT7), the overhang correction (TT8) and the two half allocations (TT9).
row.limits: Static reading of the 2.3.1 kDEF 0 (window-widgets §6 Q9: no native capture of any below-template window). Rows are conditioned on the §2.3 declared defaults: hasClose, hasZoom and collapseRequested are one runtime flag (F7), passed as present; widgetFrame set; noWidgets, collapsed, sideTitle, altWidgets, partialZoom clear; the content rect starts at the body inset (runtime policy). SWc is the TT2a declared default (SW − titleLen; a Font Manager measurement, not decoded). TT4a (anchor at 1 or N) is not reached on the corpus; Q2 (a positive anchor width after a drop with no grower) is not reached at the sampled sizes.

Window rows that stated the old default (SW − titleLen) are reworded: the kdef.window-titled-side limits, the 13 wnd# cases' title options (adding the omitted-SWc SW 60 sample) and the TT2a mutation named in the recipe-cells and half-extent rationales. transitions.priorScope: Ledger rows owned by the window family (case families: window-chrome): the single-file ledger 1.22.0 rows, with at 1.1.0 (main 1.24.0, #377) the code-10 corrections, at 1.2.0 the five corner-sprite cases extended with five procedural-frame requirements, at 1.3.0 (#412) those five cases narrowed to the procedural-frame document family, at 1.4.0 (#424) the utility frame bound to rule rows, at 1.5.0 (#432) the 13 wnd# cases re-judged against docs/spec/engine/window-widgets.md with recipe-cells and half-extent verified at the §2.3 declared defaults, and at 1.5.1 (#452) the TT2a declared default restated as SWc = SW (DECISIONS #13). row.claim: For each of the five archives, public renderWindow draws titled-utility-window, collapsed-titled-utility-window (and its legacy alias collapsed-titled-utility), side-floating-utility-window, collapsed-side-floating-utility-window (and collapsed-side-utility) and no-title-utility-window, 160 × 90 content titled 'Inspector', active and inactive, as the utility family: structure 169 × 111, 169 × 17, 179 × 99, 15 × 99 and 169 × 109 with ComposedChrome.frame insets 4/16/5/5, 4/16/5/1, 14/4/5/5, 14/4/1/5 and 4/14/5/5 (UG1–UG3, UI10; the collapsed titled bar equals the expanded one, #421 B2), and each legacy alias draws the same pixels as its canonical slug (#421 B1). Frame probes on the UFC2–UFC5, UFH7–UFH11 and UFS7–UFS11 rows and columns and the UFT3 shadow equal the drawn state's -14316/-14320 (side -14315/-14319) cicn sample points (probes where a widget glyph could land are checked only when inactive), and four points outside the structure stay untouched. When active, one 9-px period of the stripes band holds each row of the -14314 tile (side -14318, else -14314) and at least one widget box shows its -14320/-14318/-14319 ics8 glyph; when inactive the band shows only the fill P(4, 3) (side P(3, 4)) and no widget box shows a glyph pixel that differs from it. When inactive, a type that draws no title (no-title, side) shows only the fill across its whole frame interior (UW3/UW5), so a title drawn on a no-title window fails. Frame state discriminates on every archive except apple-platinum-2, whose two frame cicns are pixel-identical. collapsed-no-title-utility-window is not driven (#423). Only mask-set glyph pixels are compared; the fill outside the band, the title raster and the masked corners are not claimed.

evidence.locator:
kDEF doesn't give up when `GetResource('wnd#', d3)` returns NULL — it walks a
12-step degraded-id cascade, ANDing `d3` against a fixed mask sequence and
re-attempting until a handle resolves.
evidence.claim: GetResource(wnd#, id & mask) over twelve masks; the first non-null handle ends the cascade.
evidence.limits: Masks and landing order only. A miss reaches the no-recipe path; the runtime heuristic substitute there, base-chain ownership and Resource Manager search order are not established.

evidence.locator:
Walking gives cells **`[border[i-1], border[i])` tagged `part[i]`**
(END-based — the part code travels with the border that CLOSES the cell;
`0x5356`, confirmed in `compositor-spec.md`). Segment loop starts at index 1, so
`[0, border[0])` is the fixed leading **corner** (drawn 1:1)
evidence.claim: Segment i spans [border[i-1], border[i]) tagged part[i]; [0, border[0]) is a 1:1 corner.
evidence.limits: Cell association only; trailing-region drawing and side draw order are not established.

evidence.locator:
| 12 | **TILE** — `dstW = floor(slack/numStretch / srcW) * srcW` (whole tiles) | `0x5266`-`0x5292` |
| 8, 11, 18 | **STRETCH (grow)** — `share = sVar5/sVar6 + slack/numStretch` | `0x529e`-`0x52d6` |
| 13, 14 | **STRETCH** smaller share (`sVar5/sVar6`, no slack term) | `0x52da`-`0x52f8` |
| else | call `0x49d6(pc, fp@(24))` (the too-short byte): nonzero → leave width 0 (budget participant); else FIXED `dstW=srcW`; **except** pc∈{5,6} AND `fp@(26)`==0 → width 0 (collapse) | `0x52fc`-`0x532a` |

So **codes 5/6** (title bezel) are FIXED when the `fp@(26)` byte is nonzero
(on the title path the GetWTitle length byte `fp@(-290)`, pushed at
`0x5100`/`0x5120`; zeroed at `0x4e20` when too short and `0x4f5e` when ≤2px of
title room is left) and **collapse to 0** when it is zero —
they never grow. Budget = `slack = (srcBorder[end]−srcBorder[start-1]) − reqWidth`
(`0x518a`); the primary divisor counts only 8/11/12/18 (`0x4b3e`), while 8/11/13/14/18
share the division and whole-tile remainder. Each remainder share is truncated
against the number of recipients still to visit, so extra pixels accumulate at
the END of the walk (3/3/4 for a budget of 10 and three ordinary growers)
evidence.claim: Two-pass per-half allocation: primary 8/11/12/18, whole-tile truncation, remainder to 8/11/13/14/18 toward the end; 0x49d6 stretch verdicts leave width 0.
evidence.limits: Within one half of a given extent with a nonnegative budget. Title-anchor half extents, codes 5/6 (fp@(26) title length byte, 0x530c), widget flag values and the second too-short step (0x4e24..0x4e42) are not established. 0x49d6 receives fp@(24), the too-short byte (kdef.too-short-step).

evidence.locator: | TILE | `0x0feae` | `feae(cicn, srcRect*, dstRect*, dirByte, pixmap)` (`fp@8/12/16/20/22`) | tile along the side's run axis, one src-sized CopyBits/CopyMask per step. `dir` = anchor end, NOT axis: 1 = forward from dst top-left, 0 = reverse from dst bottom-right (`(pc==11\|\|pc==14)?0:1`). See §5.1. **Always tiles; never scales.** |
evidence.claim: Non-18 cells tile the source cell along the side, clipping the final tile. Codes 11/14 (direction byte 0) anchor at the dst end and keep the trailing source pixels in the near-end partial tile; all others anchor at the dst start.

assessments.rationale: Unknown: promotion rejected at review (see review). kdef231-reference.md §5.1 decodes the 0xfeae direction byte (pc==11||pc==14)?0:1 as the tile anchor, not the axis: 11/14 tile from the dst end (0x1018a) and every other code from the start (0x10088). The axis comes from srcH==dstH (0x10146/0x10236), with the cross axis fixed by 0x5356. The window.recipe-rules assertion checks source offset k%sw forward and sw-1-((dw-1-k)%sw) reverse for every non-18 cell, unknown-class cells included, at their runtime-placed widths. The Node test records per-archive mutation discrimination: the flip-11/14 (pre-fix) runtime fails animals and monkey-paradise; inverted-anchor and scaled runtimes fail 1990, animals, crayon-os, dolphin-som, evolution, floppies and monkey-paradise; the other six archives pass every mutation. The runtime drawTile anchors 11/14 at the far end. Limits: opaque source pixels only; opaque CopyBits under grafProcs and the CopyMask order over earlier sides are not modelled; runtime cross-axis placement and side-bar window; sampled sizes; no native capture.

assessments.rationale: Verified against the decode for this case: window.recipe-rules (source and built) replays the window-widgets layout, cell rects, title rect, WD4 pixels and HT hits for every sliced window type, both states, template + {-12,0,1,2,7,97} x {-12,0,1,33} and titles SW 0/41/300, with zero failures; in-page mutation bites (clamped budget, pinned last border, near-edge remap, kept bezels, dropped plate, skipped TT8, reversed draw order, opaque copy, painted trailing region, rect-only hit, skipped WD6, the TT2a default reverted to SW − titleLen) each fail. Limits: agreement with the static decode, not original-engine pixels (Q9); declared flag defaults (F7), content rect at the body inset (policy); the layout cache (LC1) is not reachable.

assessments.rationale: Verified narrowly for this case: every non-18 wnd# recipe cell agrees with the decoded 0xfeae tiling (kdef231-reference.md §5.1): along-run source offset k % sw for direction byte 1 and sw-1-((dw-1-k) % sw) for byte 0 (codes 11/14), cross axis 1:1, opaque source pixels, at template + {0,1,2,7,97} x {0,1,33}. The check fails for this archive under inverted-anchor and scaled blits. No 11/14 cell has a >1px non-uniform source, so the 11/14 reverse anchor is direction-neutral here and not discriminated; only the byte-1 forward anchor and tiling-vs-scaling are. Limits: agreement with the decode, not original-engine pixels; no native capture. Opaque source pixels only; opaque CopyBits under grafProcs (port+92) and the CopyMask order over earlier sides are not modelled. Cross-axis origin and placed widths come from the runtime; 0x5178 widths are a separate requirement; unknown-class cell widths are not source-determined, so their tiling is checked over the runtime-placed width only. Side bars are checked only between the top and bottom bars; overlap regions and trailing vertical regions are excluded. Sampled sizes only. The 1px LineTo fast path (0xff3e/0xffba) colour equivalence and the second byte consumer 0x6390 -> 0x11452 are not established.

assessments.rationale: Verified narrowly for this case: every non-18 wnd# recipe cell agrees with the decoded 0xfeae tiling (kdef231-reference.md §5.1): along-run source offset k % sw for direction byte 1 and sw-1-((dw-1-k) % sw) for byte 0 (codes 11/14), cross axis 1:1, opaque source pixels, at template + {0,1,2,7,97} x {0,1,33}. The check fails for this archive under inverted-anchor and scaled blits. No 11/14 cell has a >1px non-uniform source, so the 11/14 reverse anchor is direction-neutral here and not discriminated; only the byte-1 forward anchor and tiling-vs-scaling are. Limits: agreement with the decode, not original-engine pixels; no native capture. Opaque source pixels only; opaque CopyBits under grafProcs (port+92) and the CopyMask order over earlier sides are not modelled. Cross-axis origin and placed widths come from the runtime; 0x5178 widths are a separate requirement; unknown-class cell widths are not source-determined, so their tiling is checked over the runtime-placed width only. Side bars are checked only between the top and bottom bars; overlap regions and trailing vertical regions are excluded. Sampled sizes only. The 1px LineTo fast path (0xff3e/0xffba) colour equivalence and the second byte consumer 0x6390 -> 0x11452 are not established.

Limits: opaque source pixels only; opaque CopyBits under grafProcs and the CopyMask order over earlier sides are not modelled; runtime cross-axis placement and side-bar window; sampled sizes; no native capture.

assessments.rationale: Unknown: promotion rejected at review (see review). kdef231-reference.md §5.1 decodes the 0xfeae direction byte (pc==11||pc==14)?0:1 as the tile anchor, not the axis: 11/14 tile from the dst end (0x1018a) and every other code from the start (0x10088). The axis comes from srcH==dstH (0x10146/0x10236), with the cross axis fixed by 0x5356. The window.recipe-rules assertion checks source offset k%sw forward and sw-1-((dw-1-k)%sw) reverse for every non-18 cell, unknown-class cells included, at their runtime-placed widths. The Node test records per-archive mutation discrimination: the flip-11/14 (pre-fix) runtime fails animals and monkey-paradise; inverted-anchor and scaled runtimes fail 1990, animals, crayon-os, dolphin-som, evolution, floppies and monkey-paradise; the other six archives pass every mutation. The runtime drawTile anchors 11/14 at the far end. Limits: opaque source pixels only; opaque CopyBits under grafProcs and the CopyMask order over earlier sides are not modelled; runtime cross-axis placement and side-bar window; sampled sizes; no native capture.
